property: In a single command lane with fixed positive integer capacity, the number of active callbacks never exceeds that capacity.
harm: An extra callback could run while every slot is occupied and modify the same session state concurrently.
bounds: One lane with an arbitrary fixed positive integer capacity and an arbitrary finite sequence of modeled admissions and settlements.
Three inductive obligations over unbounded mathematical integers: initialization, admission, and settlement.
assumptions: The lane starts empty. Each admission uses a fresh task ID, records it before invoking its callback, and the live generation releases it once after settlement.
Capacity and generation remain fixed. The synchronous comparison and insertion are modeled as one transition.
Other admission conditions can only prevent a start; queued or blocked work leaves the active count unchanged.
exclusions: Multiple lanes and their shared budgets, resizing, resets, aborts, timeouts, and exhaustion of JavaScript task ID precision.
The solver proves the extracted transition rules. The independent replay runs the exact reported counterexample against real queue callbacks.

source.meaning: The new lane has zero active task IDs.
The source comparison supplies the admission guard in the proof.
A fresh task ID consumes one slot before the callback can run.
Settlement releases the associated slot in the same generation.
The independent replay submits callbacks through the real public queue API.

mutation.meaning: Allow another command to start when the lane is already full.
